clue.text: Play offering suggestion of boredom?

parts.note: a stage comedy whose first word, made a farce of by jumbling, would suggest the word boredom

explanation.surface: A theatre critic complains that a show was tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Alan Ayckbourn's comedy of that name; jumble the letters of its first word and you get BOREDOM, so the title itself mocks up boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known Alan Ayckbourn comedy, and the genre name for sex comedies of mistaken identity on stage.

clue.text: Work still to be done to support record

parts.note: to back is to support
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Unfinished work is piling up to back up the records.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of tasks waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: One beginning to grouse entering lair, having to stoop

indicators.note: entering puts the pieces inside the animal's home

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grouse ventures into a fox's den, having to duck its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to stoop to do something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Bow? Beacon is flickering on stern of frigate

indicators.note: flickering means unsteady and shifting, so the letters are scrambled
the stern is the rear of a ship, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A warship's signal lamp flickers at the back of the frigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' and 'stern' both look nautical, but 'Bow' is a gesture of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: An obeisance is a bow or curtsy showing respect or deference.

clue.text: Person curtailing both parts of additional discussion

indicators.note: curtailing cuts off the tail, here of each of the two words

parts.note: additional means more and discussion means talk

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short a further debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human being, someone subject to death, so any person.

clue.text: Doctor that's new, located in excellent surroundings

indicators.note: located in places the pieces inside another word

parts.note: ace means excellent
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A newly qualified doctor finds himself in very pleasant surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the atmosphere or character of a place, its setting and surroundings.

clue.text: Prominent figure in France — le blagueur

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the next words

explanation.surface: A French joker is a well-known personality in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Le blagueur is French for 'the joker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb is a celebrity, a famous person in the public eye.

clue.text: Rescue device, if river rising in centre of Charleston

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the central letters
the centre of the ten-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the river upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the famous African river

explanation.surface: A river in Charleston is flooding and someone needs saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a rope thrown to rescue a person in the water.

clue.text: Smart agent traps the rest

indicators.note: traps means catches inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a rest or short sleep

explanation.surface: A clever secret agent catches the remaining suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means smart or stylish, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Wrong article taken from historic war zone

indicators.note: something taken from a word is removed from it

parts.note: the Crimea was the scene of the 1850s Crimean War
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone flags a mistaken item removed from a former battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime is a wrong in the legal sense, an offence against the law.

clue.text: Brew of beer 'has number unwell, turning and rising

indicators.note: a brew mixes ingredients up, so the letters of beer are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning reads the pair of pieces backwards

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A drinker feels sick after a batch of homebrew, his stomach churning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brew of' rearranges BEER into REBE; 'turning' reverses NO + ILL to give LLION. The clue's last word, 'rising', is the definition, in the sense of an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt against authority, the same thing as a rebellion.

clue.text: Edges of lines covering painting?

parts.note: the outside letters of lines are L and S, read as the words 'L and S'
a cape is a cloak, a covering for the shoulders

explanation.surface: An artist puts a border of lines around the edge of a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a type of painting depicting scenery; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Buzzer, soft, framing long warning sound

indicators.note: framing means placing a border round, so the first pieces enclose the letter for long

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes
L is a common abbreviation for long, as in clothing sizes
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A doorbell buzzer, quiet but held down, gives a long warning tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short high electronic tone, used as an alert or warning signal.

clue.text: Ready to embrace fashionable petite French girl?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: game means willing or ready, as in 'game for anything'
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A trendy little French girl is ready to hug someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim, elfin girl with mischievous charm, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Ethical system? Exclamation of surprise about it after exam

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the rest

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: after puts the it after the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student gasps about their ethics test after the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is a system of principles of right and wrong conduct.

clue.text: Thinness -a blemish displayed by a lot of people?

parts.note: a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin
a city is a place of many people

explanation.surface: Being thin is described as a flaw seen in many people.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity means sparseness or shortage, the thinness of supply when something is in short measure.

clue.text: An engineer turned up for each pilot

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
an airman is a pilot

explanation.surface: An engineer arrives for every pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A repairman is a mechanic, someone whose job is fixing machines.

clue.text: Thin glow, shimmering, reveals one up late

indicators.note: shimmering means wavering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faint glow in the dark shows someone awake late.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who habitually stays up late into the night.

clue.text: Endless "True Crime" rags? There's spice

indicators.note: to rag is to tease or play about with, so the letters are messed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the phrase is dropped

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sensational true-crime tabloids are said to be spicy reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last E off 'True Crime', leaving TRUECRIM, which 'rags' rearranges. 'Rags' looks like a noun for scandal sheets but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is a yellow spice ground from the root of a ginger-family plant, used in curries.

clue.text: Example of elegance? Work to occupy that

indicators.note: to occupy is to be within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An elegant job fills that space.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is a tall formal hat worn with evening dress, a symbol of elegance.

clue.text: Type of betting? Study following odds

indicators.note: following places the study word after the odds piece

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at the start of a race
to read is to study, as in reading law at university

explanation.surface: A punter learns the odds before choosing how to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is a British racing term for the odds fixed as a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread betting is a form of wagering on whether an outcome falls above or below a quoted range.

clue.text: Opposition leader in Denmark is told to go

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
sent means told to go away

explanation.surface: Denmark's opposition leader is ordered out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent means disagreement or opposition to official opinion.

clue.text: Painter retaining grand facility for drawing?

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside

parts.note: Manet was a French Impressionist painter
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An artist keeps a fine talent for drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but here it means attracting.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet has the power to draw or attract metal objects.

clue.text: Person nearer to heaven than most in religious group?

definitions.text: Person nearer to heaven than most

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or religious
a lot is a set or group, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A member of a devout sect is supposedly closer to God than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'nearer to heaven' sound spiritual, but it is literal: a pilot flies high in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies an aircraft, so spends working hours up in the skies above most people.

clue.text: Try to lose most of the argument

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: Someone tries to drop most of the dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a game is to deliberately lose it, as in a fixed match.

clue.text: Shy in chat, sadly making bloomers

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or wretchedly, telling us to scramble the letters

explanation.surface: A timid person chatting awkwardly keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like blunders or knickers; it is flowers that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyacinths are spring flowering bulbs, so playfully things that bloom.

clue.text: No good chasing after most of this item

indicators.note: chasing after places one piece behind the other
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A useless person runs after most of this object.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an item, an object of any kind.

clue.text: One not far off? Then it's early in this!

definitions.text: One not far off? Then it's early in this!

parts.words: One not far off? Then it's early in this!
parts.note: one o'clock is just past midday, so at one you are early in the part of the day following twelve

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person is nearby and says it is still early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the time one o'clock, not a person; it is not far off noon, and is early in the period after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon runs from midday to evening, so one o'clock falls early in it.

clue.text: One offering a lot of information about a US state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the source of information goes round the article

parts.words: One offering a lot of information
parts.note: a mine of information is a person or source full of facts

explanation.surface: An expert gives a great deal of information about an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: Play in the second week of its run?

definitions.text: Play in the second week of its run?

parts.words: Play in the second week of its run?
parts.note: a play's second week of performances covers its eighth to fourteenth nights, a date in the middle of which gives a Shakespeare title

explanation.surface: A theatre production is now into its second week.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is Shakespeare's comedy; the clue reads it literally as the performance falling in nights eight to fourteen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Shakespeare comedy, named for the feast ending the Christmas season.
